registry.notes: REPLACED — Exclusion validated 2026-04-06. Betrayal as an English label was replaced by treachery (#203) as the more lexically precise term. The Greek prodotēs (traitor/betrayer) and related vocabulary carry the specific inner dynamic of hidden deliberate working against someone who trusts you — a more precise inner-being characterisation than the broader English word betrayal. Replacement registry #203 is active and Complete (1 group confirmed). The inner-being reality of betrayal is fully addressed by its replacement. No further action required.
registry.description: Betrayal is the violation of trust by someone who was trusted — the wound inflicted not by an enemy but by an ally or friend. The biblical vocabulary for this concept is folded into the words for treachery, faithlessness, and the breaking of covenant. It is one of the most theologically charged forms of relational damage because it mirrors the pattern of Israel's unfaithfulness to God. The pain of betrayal is the pain of a bond broken from the inside. [Replaced by treachery (#203).]
